node: Non-Chinese-feedstock rare earth magnets and compliant magnet supply chains
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around compliant rare-earth magnet supply chains. The strongest direct exposure is not generic rare-earth mining, but companies that can document a path from non-Chinese or allied feedstock into separated NdPr/Dy/Tb oxides, metal/alloy, and qualified NdFeB magnets. MP Materials is the reference anchor because it already combines U.S. feedstock, oxide production, magnet manufacturing, and a DoD-backed offtake/floor-price structure. The underfollowed lane includes USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels, and NioCorp: each has narrower but potentially important exposure to domestic/allied feedstock, heavy rare earths, separation, or future magnet inputs. NioCorp remains a speculative_shadow candidate because the rare-earth portion is still under evaluation and project financing/production are not yet proven. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around compliant rare-earth magnet supply chains. The strongest direct reference name is MP Materials because it has an explicit DoD-backed mine-to-magnet pathway and NdPr price-floor support. The underfollowed lane is not generic rare-earth mining; it is companies that can document non-China oxide, metal/alloy, heavy rare-earth, recycling, or qualification pathways into NdFeB or other defense-relevant permanent magnets. USA Rare Earth and Energy Fuels are the most relevant underfollowed public-market candidates found in this pass; NioCorp is a speculative-shadow candidate because its rare-earth magnet exposure is less mature than its scandium/critical-minerals defense angle.
